claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and the child or children you're enquiring about.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 18, I need to ask a couple of follow-up questions to determine eligibility, as the rules change once a child reaches 16.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, an apprenticeship, or similar)?** 

If so, could you also let me know what type of course or training they're doing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! A-levels at a sixth form college is considered approved education, which is good for eligibility purposes.

I have a couple more questions:

**Is Alex's A-level course full-time (more than 12 hours a week of supervised study/course time)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a full-time course. He's there every weekday.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more important question:

**Are you (or your partner, if applicable) responsible for Alex?** This means you're the person who is mainly looking after him and paying for things like food, clothes, and accommodation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for him. I pay for all his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Just one final question:

**When does Alex turn 19, and when is he expected to finish his A-levels?**

This is important because Child Benefit usually stops on 31 August after a child turns 19, or when they finish their approved education, whichever comes first.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 last month, so he won't be 19 until next year. He's expected to finish his A-levels in June next year, which would be before he turns 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all the details. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 18 years old (under 20)
- He is in approved education (full-time A-levels at a sixth form college)
- He lives with you
- You are responsible for him
- He will finish his A-levels in June next year, before he turns 19

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex is under 20 years old** – He is currently 18

✅ **He is in approved education** – Full-time A-levels at a sixth form college qualifies as approved education

✅ **You are responsible for him** – He lives with you and you pay for his food, clothes, and other needs

✅ **He will complete his education before turning 19** – Child Benefit will continue until he finishes his A-levels in June next year

**Important to note:** Your Child Benefit for Alex will stop when he completes his A-levels in June next year. If his circumstances change before then (for example, if he starts working 24 hours or more per week, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit), you would need to inform the Child Benefit Office as this could affect your eligibility.

If you haven't already, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
